module_title: Regulatory Bodies in Indian Education: Core Functions
introduction: This foundational level introduces the three pillars of Indian educational administration. It maps exactly what NCERT, NCTE, and NIEPA do, their target audiences (students, teachers, administrators), and their foundational mandates.

core_concepts.title: NCERT (National Council of Educational Research and Training)
core_concepts.description:
Established in 1961. It is the apex body advising the Ministry of Education on **School Education**.
- Core Function: Curriculum and textbooks. NCERT designs the National Curriculum Framework (NCF) and publishes the standard textbooks used by CBSE and various state boards.
- Target Audience: Primarily Students (by making syllabi) and Teachers (by making teaching manuals).

core_concepts.title: NCTE (National Council for Teacher Education)
core_concepts.description:
Established as a statutory body in 1993. It is the apex body for **Teacher Education**.
- Core Function: Setting standards for teacher training. NCTE decides the minimum qualifications a person needs to become a teacher (e.g., mandating B.Ed. or D.El.Ed.). It also recognizes and regulates teacher training institutes.
- Target Audience: Strictly Teachers and Teacher Education Institutes (TEIs).

core_concepts.title: NIEPA (National Institute of Educational Planning and Administration)
core_concepts.description:
Established in 1962 (originally as Asian Regional Centre for UNESCO). It is a deemed university.
- Core Function: Educational Planning, Management, and Administration. It does NOT make textbooks or train regular teachers. It trains the *leaders* of the education system.
- Target Audience: School Principals, District Education Officers (DEOs), Policy Makers, and Educational Planners.

core_concepts.title: SCERT and DIET (The State-Level Counterparts)
core_concepts.description: Just as the Center has NCERT, every State has an SCERT (State Council of Educational Research and Training) to design state-specific curricula. At the district level, this work (and primary teacher training) is handled by DIETs (District Institutes of Education and Training), which were established under NPE 1986.

important_entities.name: Statutory Body vs. Advisory Body
important_entities.key_fact: NCTE has legal power; NCERT is advisory.
important_entities.significance: A heavily tested legal distinction. NCTE is a statutory body (created by an Act of Parliament) meaning its rules on teacher qualifications are legally binding. NCERT is an autonomous advisory body; a state is technically free to reject NCERT textbooks and create its own.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If a CTET question asks: 'Which body decides the minimum qualification to become a primary school teacher?' many students choose NCERT. This is **FALSE**. NCERT only handles what the *students* learn. **NCTE** exclusively handles the qualifications and rules for *teachers*.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: NCERT for Books, NCTE for B.Ed., NIEPA for Bosses
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: NCERT = Curriculum/Books. NCTE = Teacher Training/B.Ed. NIEPA = Administration/Bosses (Principals & Planners).

exam_strategy_tips: Whenever a DSSSB question asks about an institute conducting research specifically on 'Educational Finance', 'School Mapping', or 'Micro-planning', the answer is unconditionally **NIEPA**.
